content:
Correct-target prefetch delivered the complete prefix, but this bounded screen found **no consistent latency benefit** over matched ARC demand restoration. Two 750 ms pairs were slower and one was faster. This is a scoped result for the frozen geometry and reconstructed environment, not a general rejection of prefetch.

| Seed | Demand release→first token ms | Prefetch ms | Prefetch−demand ms | Submit TTFT delta ms |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|1103|80.91|86.00|+5.09|+5.45|
|2207|73.40|84.10|+10.69|+11.13|
|3301|72.90|68.31|−4.59|−4.57|

The paired deltas span −4.59 to +10.69ms; control latencies span 72.90–80.91ms. The zero-lead pair staged nothing and restored through demand in both arms:62.35 versus65.15ms, delta +2.81ms. That single control illustrates sensitivity to scheduling/order, not an estimate of measurement variance. n=3 supports a screen only; there is no significance or confident small-effect claim. No outcome-based workload or budget changes were made.

All three primary pairs had 128 ready DRAM source blocks and **zero usable local GPU prefix blocks** at hint observation. All 128 exact prefix keys were selected and transferred:2,048 tokens/56MiB. Stage-ready occurred744.32,744.28 and744.11ms before intended demand release. This was not request-usable data: binding, destination installation and the real splice fence made it usable55.67,51.82 and39.59ms **after** intended release. Install-submit to usable was33.95,36.96 and29.88ms. Fences preceded first forward in every primary prefetch arm; all reservations and source protections were released. No allocation failures occurred. These observations do not isolate one component as the cause of each latency delta.

Both arms restored 2,048 tokens, executed 14 prompt tokens locally, and reused zero preexisting GPU prefix tokens. The preservation field called `reused_tokens` includes external loads; the analyzer explicitly subtracts loaded tokens when reporting preexisting GPU reuse. Each measured gap moved 56 MiB H2D and 0 D2H in either arm. Demand used a real demand load; prefetch used 56 MiB speculative H2D plus 56 MiB GPU staging-to-destination copying, with no demand H2D remainder. Whole-arm preparation-inclusive totals matched: 7,516,192,768 H2D bytes and58,720,256 D2H bytes. Transfer/device times are retained separately and were not added to overlapping runner time.

Staging peaked at 56 MiB; simultaneous staging+destination residency was 112 MiB inside the fixed640-block/280MiB GPU pool (one null block is unavailable). Host-observed staging byte-time was 45.03,44.81 and44.13MiB·s. This is reservation lifetime through host-observed fence acknowledgment, not a sampled physical-VRAM integral.

| Seed | Background TTFT demand→prefetch ms | Mean ITL demand→prefetch ms | Elapsed delta ms | Throughput demand→prefetch tokens/s |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|1103|28.95→33.60|15.639→15.680|+25.48|63.836→63.634|
|2207|28.99→29.18|15.691→15.702|+5.93|63.624→63.577|
|3301|30.72→31.61|15.683→15.697|+8.40|63.644→63.578|

Each background emitted 512 tokens. Throughput divides 512 by actual submit-to-stream-completion seconds (about 8.02–8.05s); mean ITL divides first-to-last token receipt interval by 511. Background decode actually spanned intended demand in every primary arm, with about 2.24–2.25s of overlapping request lifetimes. The zero-lead control released both requests together, so it verifies overlap rather than preexisting decode. All 16 measured requests and all 2,112 requests including preparation completed with zero failures. Exact output tokens and ordered key chains matched across **all 264 requests per paired arm**, including the zero-lead pair. Physical identity and selected-source-key checks passed.

Controls and provenance: cached Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct; dense BF16/TP1/block16; maxlen8192; ARC/native store_threshold2;448MiB DRAM;128-block prefetch budget; batch-invariant eager generation; fixed512-token background released100ms before128-token resume; seeds1103/2207/3301 with alternating arm order and fresh servers. Both arms received the same privileged correct-target pending hint at wait origin; release did not wait for RPC acknowledgment. Actual hint initiation was about0.11–0.16ms after origin and release lateness0.51–1.30ms in primary arms. All overhead affecting client-observed timing is included. No semantic scoring or per-step synchronized CUDA timing was enabled. Rich preservation logging remains; absolute timings need not transfer to a less instrumented serving stack.

The sole arm config difference is the new default-off diagnostic `wait_hint_diagnostic_no_dispatch`, which suppresses speculative movement in the demand arm while preserving publication/binding effects. Soft retention is off in both arms. Inherent DRAM refcount protection during actual prefetch differs; there were no competing DRAM admissions in the measured gap (0 D2H). Native threshold2 counts CPU lookups and stops on the first miss, so the initial two-warm readiness had no admitted prefix and is explicitly excluded. The validity repair froze 256 GPU-cold source requests, resetting only GPU cache while preserving DRAM, followed by six fixed distinct pressure prompts. A separate endpoint-setup readiness failure ran zero requests. Geometry, token inputs and release schedule did not change after a valid opportunity was established.

Recovery was substantial and is not an exact historical runtime reproduction. The requested extension pin was recovered through authenticated Git. The parent-supplied archive restored 4,649 authoritative source payloads; absent non-Python resources and compiled binaries were supplied by a pinned compatible prerelease wheel. All recovered payloads and 2,581 additions were rehashed after execution. The historical full Git tree is not claimed. Python3.12.13, Torch2.13.0+cu130, the wheel, local recovery baseline, extension patch, model/input pins and full dependency versions are in `evidence/final-audit.json`, `runtime-stage.json`, `runtime-overlay.json`, `environment-freeze.txt` and `frozen-screen.json`. Runtime publication utility tests passed 4/4; extension endpoint/prefetch/splice/fence/cleanup tests passed 144/144. Real readiness and paired GPU execution exercised the complete publication, idle-work, binding and install path.

Machine-readable arms, all deltas, validity and metric denominators: `evidence/screen-measurements.json` and `evidence/paired-measurements.json`. Raw logs/JSON remain losslessly compressed under `results/`; the decompressed hashes are recorded in `evidence/storage-handback.json`. Reproduction: `REPRODUCE.md`; code patch: `evidence/extension-diagnostic.patch`; task-local driver/analyzer: `opportunity_screen.py` / `analyze_screen.py`. No push or PR. Optional CPU retention simulation was not needed for this delivery screen.

Cleanup and final custody are recorded in `evidence/storage-handback.json`, `screen-restoration.json`, `screen-restoration.activity.json` and `screen-device-release.json`. The pinned reusable environment, recovered source/wheel and compressed evidence are retained. Shared model/dependency caches, historical paused work and other owners were preserved; no personal configuration was edited. See CURRENT.md for final verified ownership state.
